sentences.cn_text: 罗伯特·F·肯尼迪曾说过，一国的GDP衡量「除了使生活有价值的东西之外的一切」。随着英国投票决定脱离欧盟，且GDP已被预测将因此放缓，现在正是评估他所指何物的恰当时机。
sentences.en_text: Robert F. Kennedy once said that a country’s GDP measures “everything except that which makes life worthwhile.” With Britain voting to leave the European Union, and GDP already predicted to slow as a result, it is now a timely moment to assess what he was referring to.

sentences.cn_text: GDP及其实用性问题已困扰政策制定者超过半个世纪。
sentences.en_text: The question of GDP and its usefulness has annoyed policymakers for over half a century.

sentences.cn_text: 许多人认为它是一个有缺陷的概念。
sentences.en_text: Many argue that it is a flawed concept.

sentences.cn_text: 它衡量了无关紧要之事，却遗漏了真正重要之事。
sentences.en_text: It measures things that do not matter and misses things that do.

sentences.cn_text: 根据最新衡量标准，英国的GDP一直是西方世界艳羡的对象，失业率创历史新低，增长数据亮眼。
sentences.en_text: By most recent measures, the UK’s GDP has been the envy of the Western world, with record low unemployment and high growth figures.

sentences.cn_text: 如果一切进展顺利，那为何还有超过1700万人投票支持脱欧，尽管有警告称这可能对本国经济前景造成何种影响？
sentences.en_text: If everything was going so well, then why did over 17 million people vote for Brexit, despite the warnings about what it could do to their country’s economic prospects?

sentences.cn_text: 最近一项关于各国及其将增长转化为福祉能力的年度研究为这一问题提供了一些启示。
sentences.en_text: A recent annual study of countries and their ability to convert growth into well-being sheds some light on that question.

sentences.cn_text: 在所衡量的163个国家中，英国在确保经济增长转化为对国民有意义的改善方面表现最差。
sentences.en_text: Across the 163 countries measured, the UK is one of the poorest performers in ensuring that economic growth is translated into meaningful improvements for its citizens.

sentences.cn_text: 为更全面地评估各国表现，研究不仅关注GDP，还衡量了来自健康、教育和公民社会参与等领域的40多组不同标准。
sentences.en_text: Rather than just focusing on GDP, over 40 different sets of criteria from health, education and civil society engagement have been measured to get a more rounded assessment of how countries are performing.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管所有这些国家都面临各自的挑战，但存在一些共同主题。
sentences.en_text: While all of these countries face their own challenges, there are a number of consistent themes.

sentences.cn_text: 诚然，自2008年全球崩溃以来经济复苏已初现端倪，但在健康和教育等领域的关键指标上，主要经济体却持续下滑。
sentences.en_text: Yes, there has been a budding economic recovery since the 2008 global crash, but in key indicators in areas such as health and education, major economies have continued to decline.

sentences.cn_text: 然而并非所有国家皆是如此。
sentences.en_text: Yet this isn’t the case with all countries.

sentences.cn_text: 一些相对贫穷的欧洲国家在包括公民社会、收入平等和环境在内的各项指标上都取得了巨大进步。
sentences.en_text: Some relatively poor European countries have seen huge improvements across measures including civil society, income equality and environment.

sentences.cn_text: 这是富裕国家可以汲取的教训：当GDP不再被视为衡量国家成功的唯一标准时，世界呈现出截然不同的面貌。
sentences.en_text: This is a lesson that rich countries can learn: When GDP is no longer regarded as the sole measure of a country’s success, the world looks very different.

sentences.cn_text: 因此，肯尼迪所指的是，尽管GDP一直是衡量国家经济活动最常用的方法，但作为一种衡量标准，它已不再充分。
sentences.en_text: So, what Kennedy was referring to was that while GDP has been the most common method for measuring the economic activity of nations, as a measure, it is no longer enough.

sentences.cn_text: 它未能涵盖诸如环境质量或教育成果等重要因素——而所有这些都对个人幸福感有所贡献。
sentences.en_text: It does not include important factors such as environmental quality or education outcomes — all things that contribute to a person’s sense of well-being.

sentences.cn_text: 全球及英国预测的增长急剧下滑可能导致我们赖以维系福祉和增长的日常服务出现衰退。
sentences.en_text: The sharp hit to growth predicted around the world and in the UK could lead to a decline in the everyday services we depend on for our well-being and for growth.

sentences.cn_text: 但如果政策制定者将工作重心转向改善福祉，而非仅仅担忧GDP数据，便可能避免预测中的厄运，甚至实现进步。
sentences.en_text: But policymakers who refocus efforts on improving well-being rather than simply worrying about GDP figures could avoid the forecasted doom and may even see progress.
